correctness.rationale: The all-ordered-pairs objective equals full reciprocal-rate tour length minus the minimum holding time. A unique c-root generates a dual convex combination of maximal omitted-edge sums; Cauchy--Schwarz and the budget give the universal sharp M²/B bound, and the proposed holding times saturate both inequalities. Strict Cauchy equality and budget saturation prove global uniqueness even at ties. Exact extremal cases and 6393 deterministic finite checks corroborate but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Worst-pair first-hitting latency is a natural robust routing/transition design criterion, distinct from stationary-target average Kemeny or spectral mixing. An all-heterogeneous-price exact unique optimizer, endogenous price pooling, price-tie boundaries, sorted finite construction and sharp three-state crossover Q=2 provide a structural and practically interpretable full classification; no broader-network claims are made.
